laws.k: domestic-workers|GB|Immigration Rules, Appendix Overseas Domestic Worker
laws.t: Immigration Rules, Appendix Overseas Domestic Worker
laws.tp: Six-month visa; change of employer allowed since 2016; no extension.
laws.s2: Visa enam bulan. Sejak 2016 boleh pindah majikan, tetapi visa tidak dapat diperpanjang.

coded.vl: General labor law applies, or a dedicated statute grants its core rights
coded.n: Employment law applies, with exemptions from working-time limits and a family-worker exemption from the minimum wage.
coded.src: Employment Rights Act 1996; Working Time Regulations 1998 reg. 19

coded.fn: Written contract in a language understood
coded.vl: Written contract required and provided in a language the worker understands
coded.n: Written statement of terms from day one; the Overseas Domestic Worker visa requires written terms.
coded.src: Employment Rights Act 1996 s. 1; Immigration Rules Appendix ODW

coded.vl: A separate or lower minimum, or one set only by policy
coded.n: Minimum wage applies, except under the family-worker exemption.

coded.vl: At least monthly payment, documented, with limits on deductions or in-kind pay
Only a daily rest rule, or a longer limit than for other workers
coded.n: Daily rest applies; weekly limit and night-work rules do not.

coded.vl: At least 24 consecutive hours, not replaceable by pay at the employer's request
Equal to or longer than for other workers

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: General rule only, not specific to domestic workers or without a penalty
coded.n: General criminal law; Modern Slavery Act.

coded.vl: Accommodation standards only; living in may be required
coded.n: Accommodation offset rules; living in may be agreed.

coded.vl: Change allowed only in listed cases or after conditions are met
coded.n: May change employer within the six-month visa, which cannot be extended.

coded.vl: Worker may not be charged recruitment fees
coded.n: Employment agencies may not charge work-seekers fees.
Employment Agency Standards inspectorate; no licensing for domestic work.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
Included in the general social security system, including maternity

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence

coded.vl: May form and join trade unions

dec.n: Saadi v. the United Kingdom (Grand Chamber)
dec.pe: An Iraqi asylum seeker was held for seven days at a centre so his claim could be decided fast. The Grand Chamber said this was allowed.
dec.pi: Seorang pencari suaka Irak ditahan tujuh hari di sebuah pusat agar permohonannya cepat diputus. Majelis Agung menyatakan itu boleh.

dec.pe: A woman from Uganda said she was kept as a domestic servant in London. The police could not deal with it properly because servitude was not a crime in itself. The European Court said the UK broke the Convention. The UK had created that crime in 2010.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan dari Uganda mengaku ditahan sebagai pembantu di London. Polisi tidak bisa menanganinya dengan benar karena perhambaan belum menjadi tindak pidana tersendiri. Pengadilan HAM Eropa menyatakan Inggris melanggar Konvensi. Inggris sudah membuat tindak pidana itu pada 2010.

dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
dec.pe: A young woman from Nigeria was brought to the UK on false papers to work in a family home, abused and then thrown out. The employer said she could not sue because her work was illegal. The Supreme Court said she could.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan muda dari Nigeria dibawa ke Inggris dengan dokumen palsu untuk bekerja di rumah keluarga, dianiaya lalu diusir. Majikan berkata ia tidak bisa menggugat karena pekerjaannya ilegal. Mahkamah Agung menyatakan ia boleh menggugat.

dec.n: Taiwo v. Olaigbe; Onu v. Akwiwu
dec.ct: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
dec.pe: Two domestic workers from Nigeria were badly treated by employers who knew their visas left them with nowhere to go. They said this was race discrimination. The Supreme Court disagreed: immigration status is not race or nationality under the law.
dec.pi: Dua pekerja rumah tangga dari Nigeria diperlakukan buruk oleh majikan yang tahu visa mereka membuat mereka tidak punya pilihan. Mereka menyebutnya diskriminasi ras. MA tidak setuju: menurut hukum, status imigrasi bukan ras atau kewarganegaraan.

dec.pe: Moroccan women employed as cooks and domestic staff at embassies in London were refused their wage claims because the embassies claimed immunity. The Supreme Court let the claims go ahead.
dec.pi: Perempuan Maroko yang bekerja sebagai juru masak dan staf rumah tangga di kedutaan di London tidak bisa menuntut upah karena kedutaan mengklaim kekebalan. MA mengizinkan gugatan berlanjut.

dec.n: V.C.L. and A.N. v. the United Kingdom
dec.pe: Two Vietnamese teenagers found working on cannabis farms in England were prosecuted instead of being treated as trafficking victims. The Court said this broke the Convention.
dec.pi: Dua remaja Vietnam yang ditemukan bekerja di ladang ganja di Inggris dituntut alih-alih diperlakukan sebagai korban perdagangan orang. Mahkamah menyatakan ini melanggar Konvensi.

dec.pe: A Filipino woman said she worked almost all day for a diplomat’s family in London, without pay and without her passport. The Supreme Court said the diplomat could not use immunity to avoid her claim.
dec.pi: Seorang perempuan Filipina mengaku bekerja hampir sepanjang hari untuk keluarga diplomat di London, tanpa upah dan tanpa paspornya. MA menyatakan diplomat itu tidak bisa memakai kekebalan untuk menghindari gugatannya.
